clue.text: Pad that goes with a nick?

definitions.text: Pad that goes with a nick?

parts.words: Pad that goes with a nick?
parts.note: pad is slang for a home and nick is British slang for a police station, so this is the building attached to one

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang 'the nick' is a police station (also prison), and 'pad' is a place to live.
explanation.definitionFit: A police building, historically with living quarters, is the home that comes with a police post.

clue.text: Figure raised after a heavy fall?

definitions.text: Figure raised after a heavy fall?

parts.words: Figure raised after a heavy fall?
parts.note: a figure built up by children once a thick layer of snow has come down

explanation.definitionFit: Children build a human figure out of snow once plenty has fallen.

clue.text: Country with unusual lager-first-class to knock back!

indicators.note: unusual lager is lager in an odd arrangement of its letters
to knock back is to drink down, here meaning to turn the term for first-class around

parts.note: A1 (written AI) means first-class

explanation.surface: A nation where strange beer is the top drink to down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges LAGER into ALGER; 'to knock back' turns AI round to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: A North African nation on the Mediterranean.

clue.text: To understand Pinter play, retell the first half

indicators.note: play here means rework, so the letters of Pinter are arranged differently
only the opening three of retell's six letters are used

explanation.surface: Advice to grasp a Harold Pinter play by retelling half of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' rearranges PINTER as INTERP; 'the first half' of RETELL is RET.
explanation.definitionFit: To construe or make sense of something is to grasp its meaning.

clue.text: Soundly criticises notches on arrows

indicators.note: soundly here means as heard, so a word for criticises is said out loud

parts.note: knocks means criticises

explanation.surface: Someone thoroughly finds fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like 'thoroughly' but signals a sound-alike: KNOCKS, with silent K.
explanation.definitionFit: The notch at the end of an arrow that grips the bowstring is its nock.

clue.text: No realist, he, driving chariots with no acceleration

indicators.note: driving suggests churning about, so the remaining letters are jumbled
with no means a letter is dropped from chariots

parts.note: a is the physics symbol for acceleration

explanation.surface: A charioteer who is no realist, racing without speeding up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes A from CHARIOTS to leave CHRIOTS, which 'driving' rearranges. The bird is proverbially said to bury its head in the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird supposedly hides its head in sand, so it typifies someone refusing to face facts.

clue.text: Academic whose mate arrives early on board?

definitions.text: Academic whose mate arrives early on board?

parts.words: Academic whose mate arrives early on board?
parts.note: a learned person, and also the name of a quick four-move checkmate in chess

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' is the chess checkmate; the 'Scholar's mate' wins in four moves, early on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person in academia; the chess term names a very fast checkmate.

clue.text: The case for arms limitation

parts.note: reads like a disarmament argument but describes a garment restraining a person's arms

explanation.definitionFit: A restraining garment with long sleeves tied to stop the wearer using their arms.

clue.text: Brainwork, however tiring to begin

parts.note: though can mean however

indicators.note: to begin picks the opening letter of tiring

explanation.surface: Mental effort, though it is tiring at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental activity or reasoning is work done by the mind.

clue.text: Reach and pass the sauce

definitions.meaning: to draw level with and overtake
an old variant spelling of ketchup

explanation.surface: Asking someone at the table to stretch over and hand on the sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw level with a rival; and a variant spelling of the tomato condiment ketchup.

clue.text: Groundsman's ideal ability to name a note

definitions.meaning: a groundsman tends a sports field, and the best playing surface is a flawless one
the gift of identifying a musical note without a reference

explanation.surface: A groundskeeper also has a musician's gift for identifying notes.
explanation.walkthrough: A pitch is a cricket or football playing surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A flawless playing field; and the musical gift of identifying notes unaided.

clue.text: Lover is married, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of married are disordered

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is, unfortunately, already wed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who adores another is an ardent fan or suitor.

clue.text: One who checks filters, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that filters may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Someone inspects filters, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: One who suppresses or smothers something holds it in check.

clue.text: Chinese society joining a Pacific kingdom

parts.note: a tong is a Chinese secret society

explanation.surface: A Chinese association joins a South Seas island monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Polynesian island nation ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: First at Epsom-or chaser, perhaps?

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters may be arranged differently
first at picks the opening letter of Epsom

explanation.surface: A winner at Epsom races, or a steeplechaser.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom is an English racecourse, home of the Derby; a chaser is a horse that runs steeplechases.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughbred bred for running at meetings such as Epsom.

clue.text: A beefy dish's means of dating at a party

parts.note: carbon dating fixes the age of old material
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A meat dish served at a party gives a way to get dates.
explanation.definitionFit: A grilled or stewed meat preparation.

clue.text: Pilot's instrument shows season in change

indicators.note: in places the season word inside the change word

parts.note: alter means change
time can mean a season, a period

explanation.surface: An aviation gauge shows the weather is changing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockpit gauge showing height above ground.

clue.text: She rate, perhaps, as a saint?

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters of she rate may be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether a woman ranks among saints.
explanation.definitionFit: St Teresa of Avila, a Spanish mystic venerated as holy.

clue.text: Mum caber-tossing? How gruesome!

parts.note: ma means mum

indicators.note: tossing throws the letters of caber about

explanation.surface: Mother throwing a caber at the Highland Games is a grim sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Tossing the caber, a long log, is a Scottish Highland Games sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghastly and dwelling on death or horror.

clue.text: Exhibition a blot on the landscape?

explanation.surface: A show that spoils the view.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectacle to look at; also something ugly, as in 'you look a fright'.

clue.text: Bread picked up by the beak!

definitions.text: Bread picked up by the beak!

parts.words: Bread picked up by the beak!
parts.note: bread is slang for money and beak is British slang for a magistrate, so this is a magistrate's pay

explanation.walkthrough: 'Beak' is British slang for a magistrate; a paid magistrate is a stipendiary. The surface pictures a bird pecking crumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed salary or allowance, as paid to a stipendiary magistrate.

clue.text: He seizes Greek sailor. Lubber? Not half!

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: not half keeps only the back half of lubber

explanation.surface: A Greek sailor grabs a clumsy landlubber.
explanation.walkthrough: A lubber is a clumsy sailor; 'Not half' drops LUB.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who snatches or grasps things.

clue.text: What is seen below skirt? Can peek, cheekily!

indicators.note: cheekily suggests mischief, so the letters of can peek are mixed up

explanation.surface: A naughty glimpse under a skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: The bone over the knee joint shows under a short hem.

clue.text: Length of composition

definitions.meaning: a portion, as of cloth or string

explanation.surface: How long a musical work is.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut portion of material; also a single musical work.

clue.text: Folding sheets, Japanese fashion

parts.note: reads like laundry but means the craft of shaping paper sheets

explanation.definitionFit: The traditional Japanese craft of paper-folding into models.

clue.text: Bert lame, perhaps, but without a quiver

indicators.note: perhaps signals that bert lame is rearranged, with the letter of the word a left over and dropped

explanation.surface: Bert is lame but does not shake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges BERT LAME, and 'without a' leaves its A out. The verb 'quiver' is the definition, not an arrow case.
explanation.definitionFit: To shake or shiver slightly.

clue.text: Doctor after drink in charge, still?

indicators.note: after places the doctor letters behind the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor in charge after a drink, is he still?
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' is a noun: a distilling apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: An old distilling apparatus used by alchemists.

clue.text: Sounds from here of pate being opened by judge

indicators.note: being opened suggests pate broken up and laid out afresh

parts.note: a recorder is a type of judge in England

explanation.surface: Noises come from a head split open by a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: A Recorder is a part-time judge in English courts.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that plays back recorded noises.
